Branch Manager,

Sheelavant vs Dhanasingh And Anr
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: This appeal is by the injured claimant aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 01.09.2016 passed in MVC No.1160/2014 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.III, Vijaypur, by which the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition filed by the claimant under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act negating his claim with regard to the road traffic accident in which he suffered the injuries, merely because there was delay in filing the FIR.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.III, Vijaypur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The facts leading to filing of the present appeal are that, on 21.04.2014 at about 10.30 a.m.,
appellant was proceeding on a motorcycle as a pillion rider.
The rider of the said motorcycle was attempting to overtake the tractor and trailer bearing Reg. No.KA-28/TB-0579- 0580.

The driver of the said tractor and trailer though gave signal, while the rider of the motorcycle was in the process of overtaking, the driver of the said tractor and trailer again came back on to the road colliding with the motorcycle resulting in the accident causing injuries to the appellant.
The appellant suffered fractural injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Civil Hospital at Indi and thereafter he was shifted to Dr.B.K.Prani Hospital, Miraj, where he took treatment as inpatient and had spent Rs.2,00,000/-
towards the treatment.

Thereupon, claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act contending that he was earning Rs.7,000/- per month as a coolie and due to injuries sustained, he NC: 2023:KHC-K:8627 was not in a position to work.
As such, he claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.

Sheelavant vs Dhanasingh And Anr on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187183746/
2 3.
Upon service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and placed ex-parte.
Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company appeared though its counsel and filed statement of objections, denying the mode and manner of accident.
However, it is admitted that the tractor in question had been insured with the Insurance Company.
It is contended that it was a self accident caused by the claimant himself being the rider of the motorcycle.
It is also contended that there was no damage to the motorcycle and the tractor and trailer.
Therefore, it is contended that the claim made by the claimant was false and fabricated.
4. On the basis of the pleadings, the Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence.
The claimant examined himself as PW.1 and one Dr.S.S.Nagathan as PW.2 and 17 documents were marked NC: 2023:KHC-K:8627 as Exs.P1 to P17.

No witnesses have been examined on behalf of the respondents except marking copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R1.
5.

The Tribunal on appreciation of the pleadings and evidence, dismissed the claim petition on the premise that the claimant has suppressed the true and actual facts of the matter and that there was no explanation for the delay in filing the complaint and that the versions of the complaint was not reliable.
Accordingly, dismissed the claim petition.
6. Being aggrieved by the same appellant is before this Court.

7. Sri Sanganagouda B. Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellant at the outset drawing attention of this Court to the document at Ex.P7 submits that Doctor at Miraj Hospital where the claimant was treated had filed MLC by informing Miraj Police Station over phone that is NC:
2023:KHC-K:8627 on 22 04.2014 at 5:00 p.m., instant.
He further submits that Ex.P7 records the injured having been admitted with the history of road traffic accident at Indi at 11:30 p.m., on 21.04.2014.

He submits that the said document is sufficient enough to show that necessary and required steps in informing the concerned police with regard to the accident having taken place and complied and nothing else was required to be done on the part of the claimant.

That it was the duty of the concerned jurisdictional police, who was required to record the statement of claimant on receipt of MLC and that not having been done, the claimant cannot be held responsible.
He further submits that the complaint was filed on 04.05.2014 by the brother of the injured as the injured-claimant was not in a position of file the complaint.
Thus he submits that there is no abnormality in the process of lodging the complaint and the delay is self explanatory.
Hence, seeks for allowing of the appeal and to set aside the order of the Tribunal.

Per contra, Smt. Anuradha M. Desai, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company drawing attention of this Court to the contents of the complaint and the portion of the cross-examination of the claimant submits that the reasons for the delay in lodging the complaint has not been satisfactorily examined.

Referring to the reasoning assigned by the Tribunal with regard to the delay in filing the complaint she submits that the Tribunal has assessed the material evidence from all angles and no infirmity or irregularity can be found with the same, hence, seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

Sheelavant vs Dhanasingh And Anr on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187183746/
3 9.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
10. There may not be dispute with regard to the injuries sustained by the claimant as found in the Wound Certificate at Ex.P4.
There cannot also be any doubt with regard to the injured taking treatment at Indi Hospital, Solapur Hospital as well as Miraj Hospital.
There may not be any doubt even with regard to Ex.P7 of MLC having NC: 2023:KHC-K:8627 been filed by the Miraj Hospital.

The pertinent question which required to be looked into is whether the injuries were caused in the accident that allegedly took place on 21.04.2014 involving the offending Tractor and Trailer bearing registration No.KA-28/TB-0579-0580.
The Tribunal on assessing the material evidence has come to the conclusion that the delay in filing the complaint was only to deliberate and to implicate the offending Tractor.

As rightly taken note of by the Tribunal, Ex.P7 - MLC cannot be relied upon as a stand alone document to justify the claim of the claimant of he suffering injuries on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending Tractor and Trailer by its driver.

As mentioning of the Tractor and Trailer with a registration number has surfaced for first time in the complaint filed by the brother of the claimant-injured on 04.05.2014 and there has been no whisper of the involvement of the said Tractor and Trailer prior to the said complaint.

The Tribunal also has taken note of the fact that accident has allegedly taken place in front of the Panchayat Office and it was highly NC:
2023:KHC-K:8627 improbable that said accident would have gone unnoticed for such a long period between 21.04.2014 to 04.05.2014.

Another aspect which the Tribunal has taken note of is that in the complaint the complainant has stated that after injured-claimant regained his conscious he has narrated details of the incident involving the Tractor.
The Tribunal has just opposed contents of the said complaint with Ex.P7, in which, it is stated by the patient was "conscious and was having BP 130/80".
As such the theory of injured-claimant being unconscious for such a long period has been negated by the Tribunal.

11. It may be pertinent at this juncture refer to the cross-examination of the injured-claimant, in which, at Para 2 he has admitted that he is the owner of the motorcycle which was involved in the accident, the said motorcycle was not registered and he was not having any Driving License.

At Para No.3 of the deposition, he has admitted that that the Tractor and Trailer was going ahead of his motorcycle and when his motorcycle came on to the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8627 right side of the said Tractor and Trailer, the Trailer portion brushed the motorcycle, resulting in he falling on to his right side and sustained injuries to his left leg.
In the complaint and in the charge-sheet however it is stated that the claimant sustained injuries on account of the wheel of the Trailer running over his left leg.
Contemplation of these facts of the case and evidence on record would not meet the logic.
If the claimant had fallen on to the right side account of the Trailer hitting the motorcycle, the wheel of the Trailer running over his left leg becomes questionable.
That apart the IMV report at Ex.P3 would revel that there was no visible damage to the motorcycle.

Yet another aspect to be seen is that in the photograph produced at Ex.P3 - injury is shown to be on the right leg below knee while in the Wound Certificate and the Disability Certificate injury is shown to be to the lower limb of the left leg.

From aforesaid records and evidence it is clear that an attempt has been made to create and build a false evidence as rightly Sheelavant vs Dhanasingh And Anr on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187183746/
4 taken note of by the Tribunal while dismissing claim petition.
In that - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8627 view of the matter no infirmity or legality can be found in the reasoning given by the Tribunal.
12. No grounds are made out warranting interference.
Appeal is dismissed.
